For the expression to be defined modulo \(20\), both \(a^{-1}\) and \((a-1)^{-1}\) must exist. That requires

\[
\gcd(a,20)=1 \quad\text{and}\quad \gcd(a-1,20)=1.
\]

But \(a\) and \(a-1\) are consecutive integers, so one of them is even. Since \(20\) is even, an even number cannot be relatively prime to \(20\). Therefore, it is impossible for both \(a\) and \(a-1\) to have inverses modulo \(20\).

So there are no integers \(a\) satisfying the condition.
